meta.untested: Any receptor in receptors.json that is not listed for an odorant has not been tested with it.

WM.note: Common variant with two substitutions, R88W and T133M.

genotypes.perception: More sensitive; more often unpleasant (group result).
Less sensitive and less unpleasant than RT/RT (group result).
Less sensitive and less unpleasant than RT/RT (group result).

cases.perception: Androstenone is perceived by different people as offensive (“sweaty, urinous”), pleasant (“sweet, floral”) or odourless. People with RT/WM or WM/WM genotypes were, as a group, less sensitive to androstenone and found it less unpleasant than the RT/RT group.

conflict.text: Mainland et al. 2015 reported a response of the WM haplotype with a log EC50 of about −5 (whole-log value). M2OR therefore marks this pair as inconclusive; the simulation follows Keller et al. 2007, the study that links genotype to perception.

expression.text: Each olfactory sensory neuron expresses one allele of its receptor gene (monoallelic expression, shown in rodents). A heterozygote is therefore modelled as half of the neurons for this receptor carrying each allele.

T113A+R226Q.note: Haplotype carrying both T113A and R226Q.

cases.perception: T113A and R226Q each impair the response of OR2J3 to cis-3-hexen-1-ol and together abolish it in vitro. The haplotype containing both explains 26.4% of the variation in cis-3-hexen-1-ol detection in the study cohort.

expression.text: Each olfactory sensory neuron expresses one allele of its receptor gene (monoallelic expression, shown in rodents). A heterozygote is therefore modelled as half of the neurons for this receptor carrying each allele.

APT (2 aa).note: Differs from the reference by 2 amino acids; slightly more sensitive to guaiacol, but the effect is small.

VLT (5 aa).note: Differs by 5 amino acids; much lower affinity, but still responds significantly.

ALI (8 aa).note: Differs by 8 amino acids; not significantly different from vector-only control cells (p = 0.11), i.e. non-functional in this assay.

genotypes.perception: Each copy of the reference allele raised perceived intensity by about 2.1 ranks (β = 2.10).
One reference copy (+2.1 ranks intensity) and one VLT copy (−2.4 ranks intensity, +3.3 ranks valence, i.e. less unpleasant).
One reference copy (+2.1 ranks intensity) and one ALI copy (−4.3 ranks intensity, +3.7 ranks valence).
Each copy of VLT lowered perceived intensity by about 2.4 ranks and raised valence by about 3.3 ranks (β = −2.39; β = 3.33).
Each copy of ALI lowered perceived intensity by about 4.3 ranks and raised valence by about 3.7 ranks (β = −4.34; β = 3.71) — the weakest and least unpleasant percept of guaiacol.

cases.perception: OR10G4 allele type explained 15.4% of the variance in perceived intensity of guaiacol and 10.3% of the variance in perceived valence (n = 308). It did not explain perception of the lower-affinity agonists vanillin and ethyl vanillin.
